title: MicrowaveClear
question: How does a microwave oven work?
hook: A microwave oven is a radio transmitter in a metal box. Electrons whirl in a magnetron to make 12 cm waves that twist water molecules 2.45 billion times a second. Take one apart in 3D and find the hot spots.

explainer.title: A radio transmitter in a metal box
explainer.text: A transformer, a capacitor and a diode turn mains electricity into about 4,000 volts. That powers a magnetron, which makes microwaves. A metal duct called the waveguide pipes them into the cooking box, whose metal walls bounce them around until the food soaks them up.

explainer.title: Electrons whirling past copper cavities
explainer.text: In the magnetron, electrons boil off a hot cathode and rush towards a copper anode. Strong magnets bend their paths so they swirl past ten little cavities, which ring like whistles 2.45 billion times a second. The waves are about 12.2 cm long, and about 65% of the power going in comes out as microwaves.

explainer.title: Twisting water molecules
explainer.text: Water molecules have a positive end and a negative end. The microwave field flips 2.45 billion times a second, twisting them back and forth against their neighbours, and that jostling is heat. Ice molecules are locked in a crystal and barely absorb, which is why defrosting is so uneven.

explainer.title: It doesn't cook from the inside out
explainer.text: In wet food, most of the microwave power is used up in the outer 1 to 2 cm. The middle warms more slowly as heat conducts inwards, which is why recipes tell you to stir or let food stand.

explainer.title: Hot spots 6 cm apart
explainer.text: Waves bouncing between the walls add up into a standing wave with hot and cold spots about half a wavelength, 6 cm, apart. The turntable carries the food through them. Measure the melted spots on a chocolate bar and you can work out the speed of light.

explainer.title: Safe by design, and 50% means on and off
explainer.text: The door's mesh holes are about 1 to 2 mm across, far too small for a 12 cm wave to squeeze through, and interlock switches cut the power when it opens. On most ovens, 50% power means full power switched on and off; inverter ovens can really turn the magnetron down.

concepts.def: A vacuum tube where electrons, bent by magnets, swirl past resonant cavities and make microwaves.
A hollow metal duct that carries microwaves from the magnetron to the cooking cavity.
How many times a second a wave repeats. Microwave ovens use 2.45 GHz, 2.45 billion times a second.
The length of one cycle of a wave: its speed divided by its frequency. About 12.2 cm in a microwave oven.
Heating by a rapidly flipping electric field that twists polar molecules such as water against their neighbours.
How far microwaves reach into a material before most of their power is used up: about 1.7 cm in water.
A wave pattern that stays in place, made when waves reflect and overlap, with fixed hot spots and nodes.
A switch that only lets the oven run while the door is fully closed.
The share of time something is switched on. 50% power on a classic oven means on half the time.
